MONDO:0980940.name: UNC13A-related congenital neurodevelopmental disorder with epilepsy
MONDO:0980940.why_chosen: Scouted before; every earlier hit was an ALS organization or a curation consortium. A deliberate test that ALS membership is not inferred.
MONDO:0980940.notes: The 2025 discovery paper (Nature Genetics) reports about 50 patients; no family organization was found in search results or on the pages checked. Honest outcome: no group found yet.
searched: web search: UNC13A neurodevelopmental disorder families patient group

rejected.name: ALS and motor neurone organizations (Target ALS, My Name'5 Doddie Foundation, MND Association, TRICALS)
rejected.reason: UNC13A is an ALS risk gene, but these organizations serve ALS. The developmental disorder is a different condition; the earlier scout listed them anyway and the reviewer rejected them.

MONDO:0030909.name: CNKSR2-related intellectual disability with epilepsy
MONDO:0030909.why_chosen: Scouted before; eight organizations were named and none survived. A published cohort describes a family-driven CNKSR2 support group, so a group likely exists.
MONDO:0030909.notes: The BMC Medical Genomics 2021 cohort paper (PMC8281706) thanks an 'international CNKSR2 Family Support Group', but no official website for it was found. Unresolved gap: a lead for a person who can ask the paper's authors or the platform.
searched: web search: "CNKSR2" family support group website

rejected.name: Rareshare CNKSR2 community
rejected.reason: a forum on a general platform, hosted by a third party; not itself a patient organization, and its page text is mostly a copied study abstract and a parent's post

rejected.name: Human Disease Genes (humandiseasegenes.nl)
rejected.reason: information service; the atlas already lists this category as not a community

MONDO:0013464.name: Episodic ataxia type 5
MONDO:0013464.why_chosen: Scouted before with nothing found. The National Ataxia Foundation very likely serves it, but the evidence is a PDF.
MONDO:0013464.notes: The National Ataxia Foundation's episodic ataxia page redirects to a PDF listing EA1 to EA8 (https://www.ataxia.org/wp-content/uploads/2017/07/Episodic-Ataxia.pdf). The staging fetcher, like the existing scout, archives HTML only, so no quote could be archived. The homepage speaks of Ataxia in general and does not name episodic ataxia. Promising but unproven; the lead would need PDF text support in the source archive to import it.
searched: web search: National Ataxia Foundation episodic ataxia type 5 CACNB4
web search: ataxia.org episodic ataxia types National Ataxia Foundation

MONDO:0014517.name: STX1B-related generalized epilepsy with febrile seizures plus
MONDO:0014517.why_chosen: Scouted before; the only result was an information service. Same SNARE neighborhood as the first campaign.
MONDO:0014517.notes: Only clinical literature found (49 patients in 23 families). No group found.
searched: web search: STX1B epilepsy patient group families foundation

rejected.name: STXBP1 Foundation
rejected.reason: STXBP1 is a different gene (the search engine suggested it for STX1B); the foundation does not serve STX1B families

MONDO:0013523.name: BANF1-related Nestor-Guillermo progeria syndrome
MONDO:0013523.why_chosen: Scouted before; only an information service was listed. Progeria is a strong atlas example, so checking whether the family-facing progeria group covers this form matters.
MONDO:0013523.notes: Search found NORD, GARD and Orphanet reference pages only. The Progeria Research Foundation's live site returns 403 to automated visitors, so its pages were not read for any mention of Nestor-Guillermo or progeroid syndromes. Unresolved: worth asking the foundation whether it serves progeroid syndromes beyond HGPS.
searched: web search: Nestor-Guillermo progeria syndrome patient organization

MONDO:0032784.name: CACNA1B-related neurodevelopmental disorder with seizures and nonepileptic hyperkinetic movements
MONDO:0032784.why_chosen: Scouted before; only curation consortia and panels were found. Very rare (biallelic, a handful of families), a good test of 'no group yet'.
MONDO:0032784.notes: Only literature found (AJHG 2019 and later cases). No group found, consistent with a condition reported in very few families.
searched: web search: CACNA1B family foundation neurodevelopmental disorder
